items.stem: A robot must stop when a person steps into its area. Which design best ensures this behaviour?

options.text: A closed-loop system using presence sensors that feed back to halt motion
options.rationale: Correct: closed-loop feedback from presence sensing lets the robot react to the unplanned event.

options.text: An open-loop sequence timed to the normal cycle
options.rationale: Open-loop timing cannot react to an unexpected person entering the area.

options.text: A faster motor so the task finishes before anyone arrives
options.rationale: Speed does not provide safety against people entering the workspace.

options.text: Removing all sensors to simplify the controller
options.rationale: Removing sensing eliminates the feedback needed to stop safely.

items.explanation: Correct: closed-loop feedback from presence sensing lets the robot react to the unplanned event.

items.stem: Which TWO belong to the 'sense' and 'act' parts of the sense-plan-act loop respectively? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A camera detecting an object's position is part of 'sense'
options.rationale: Correct: perception via a camera is sensing.

options.text: A motor moving the gripper to the object is part of 'act'
options.rationale: Correct: driving actuators to affect the world is acting.

options.text: Choosing which object to pick next is sensing
options.rationale: Deciding the next action is 'plan', not 'sense'.

options.text: Converting sensor data into a world model is acting
options.rationale: Building a model from sensor data is sensing/perception, not acting.

items.explanation: Correct: perception via a camera is sensing.

items.stem: Why does a robot need defined coordinate frames?

options.text: So positions sensed in one frame can be transformed into the frame needed to act
options.rationale: Correct: frames let the robot relate sensor, tool and world positions consistently.

options.text: Because frames make the motors spin faster
options.rationale: Frames are a geometric bookkeeping tool, not a speed control.

options.text: Because without frames a robot cannot be powered on
options.rationale: Power-up does not depend on coordinate frames.

options.text: Because frames replace the need for any sensors
options.rationale: Frames organise spatial data but do not replace sensing.

items.explanation: Correct: frames let the robot relate sensor, tool and world positions consistently.
